ca_west_face_of_the_lamb.blurb: A small dome beside the road in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite, sitting at roughly 8,600 feet, with this being its western side. About eighteen routes, mostly trad with a few bolted lines, spread from 5.9 through the 5.10s and 5.11s, plus one 5.13. Several lines go for multiple pitches and blend cracks with face moves, while a couple of bolted lines are short. Direct sun reaches the face by midday in summer, so an early start is kind. The trail in is faint and winds through trees, and finding the best line on a first visit takes extra time.

ca_1_schultz_s_ridge.blurb: A cragging wall on the north side of Yosemite Valley, close to the El Capitan picnic area at about 4,100 feet. Bolted single pitches and trad lines are split evenly among its eighteen routes. Most fall in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a couple of 5.9s and a few at 5.12 and 5.13, so it suits climbers past the beginner stage. A handful of lines run to several pitches. Trails cross the road and wander through woods to the base; budget extra time for the longest, steepest walk. Rockfall off El Capitan in recent years left fresh talus below the wall.

ca_sunday_matinee_wall.blurb: A short wall at the western end of The Corridors, a row of rock blades in the Alabama Hills outside Lone Pine, at around 4,700 feet. Mostly bolted face routes about thirty feet tall, with a handful of trad lines and a few top-rope options. Grades run from 5.5 to 5.11 and cluster at 5.10. The climbing is steep and technical, edging on small holds with bolts placed close together, and the rock is crumbly enough that bits can rain on the leader. The base is flat and the stroll from the dirt lot is short, which makes this a decent quick session.

ca_sespe_gorge_black_wall.blurb: A roadside sandstone wall in Sespe Gorge on Highway 33 north of Ojai, at about 3,600 feet. Nearly all of its eighteen routes are trad, along with one bolted line and one boulder traverse. Most are moderate, between 5.5 and 5.7, with a few harder lines from 5.9 to 5.11. The terrain is low-angle cracks and slabs. Two crack lines take almost all of the traffic, while quieter ones can be loose and vegetated. Bolted rappel stations make the way down quick, though most routes need two ropes. The sun hits the wall for much of the day, with shade creeping in later, and the walk from the car is about a minute.

ca_west_face_4.blurb: A tall wall of roughly 700 feet on the west side of Power Dome, rising above Helms Creek canyon just under the dam at Courtright Reservoir in the southern Sierra, at about 7,700 feet. Nearly all of its eighteen routes are long alpine-style, multi-pitch climbs, graded mostly 5.9 and 5.10, with a few easier lines at 5.7 and 5.8 and a couple at 5.11. Much of the terrain is slab, and some of the older lines have long runouts between bolts; other routes mix in cracks and corners with a more reasonable bolt count.
